public_rationale: The first half is true. These firms have big non-AI businesses that make money. The test is 'AI is not doing it.' In its Q3 2025 earnings remarks, Alphabet said AI revenue was 'a key driver' of Google Cloud's faster growth. It said revenue from products built on its generative AI models grew more than 200% from a year earlier. It also said its AI products were lifting Cloud operating margins. Earlier in 2025, Microsoft said its AI business had passed a $13 billion annual revenue run rate. On the plain reading, AI was making these companies real money by late 2025, at least at Alphabet and Microsoft. That remains true even if most of their profit still came from other products. So the claim as stated is contradicted.
limitations: The companies do not report AI profit on its own. If 'making them money' means net profit from AI after its huge capital costs, the claim cannot be checked either way.
The decisive evidence is company-reported earnings call commentary, not audited segment data.
The evidence is strongest for Alphabet. Amazon and Meta were not checked against primary sources.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta make their money from non-AI products, not from AI.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta all have other products that are making them money. AI is not doing it,

from_speaker: all have other products that are making them money
every single stock you see 'growing because of AI' ... is actually growing because of something else
our_interpretation: Plain reading: at the time of the post, AI products were not a real source of revenue or profit for these four companies. Their money came from other products.
The first half (they have other money-making products) is uncontroversial. The test is the second half, 'AI is not doing it'.

He describes an ongoing state and names no period. So we use the most recent quarter the companies had reported before the post: calendar Q3 2025 (July to September 2025), reported in late October 2025.

Because 'AI is not doing it' covers all four together, clear company-reported evidence that AI was a key driver of revenue and margin at even one of them in that quarter contradicts it. Claims that AI drives earnings are company-reported. The firms do not report AI profit as a separate line.
criteria.support_condition: Company disclosures for Q3 2025 show AI products produced no meaningful revenue or profit at these companies, with growth coming from non-AI products.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Company disclosures for Q3 2025 show AI products producing meaningful, growing revenue, or named as a key driver of revenue or margin growth, at one or more of the four companies.
